transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi Doctor. I'm here today because I've been really struggling with focusing and making careless mistakes, especially at work. It feels like I constantly miss small details no matter how hard I try to pay attention.
Do you also find yourself being unusually restless, fidgety, interrupting others, or acting before thinking, or is it mainly trouble focusing and missing details?

Yes, I actually struggle with both. Besides losing focus and making careless mistakes, I frequently find myself interrupting others when they're talking. I also have a really hard time staying quiet or still, even when I'm just trying to relax and enjoy my free time.
Have these attention and restlessness symptoms been present since childhood or early adolescence, and have they been going on for at least 6 months?
Yes, they have been going on consistently for about a year and a half now. Looking back, these struggles definitely started during my childhood, well before I turned 12.
Do these symptoms cause problems in more than one area of your life, such as work, home, or relationships?

Yes, they definitely affect multiple areas of my life. At work and home, I have a really hard time following through on instructions and finishing my tasks or chores. On top of that, my habit of interrupting and butting into conversations has caused some real tension in my relationships.

latest_inference.note: Previously the only candidate was Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation). The new history supports this diagnosis strongly: the patient has both inattentive symptoms (careless mistakes, poor focus, difficulty following through) and hyperactive/impulsive symptoms (restlessness, interrupting, difficulty staying still), with onset in childhood, duration well over 6 months, and impairment across work, home, and relationships. No evidence was introduced to suggest an alternative diagnosis, so the candidate list remains the same.

Generalized Anxiety Disorder and Major Depressive Disorder are also on the differential because anxiety or low mood can impair concentration and cause mistakes, but there is not yet enough information to confirm either.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports persistent inattention (careless mistakes, poor focus, difficulty following through, incomplete tasks) and hyperactive/impulsive symptoms (interrupting others, difficulty staying still/quiet). Symptoms began in childhood, have lasted over 6 months, and cause impairment across work, home, and relationships, supporting ADHD combined presentation.
